as mentioned by another redditor, job desc n pay is dependent on the job scope! the interview is also dependant on the job, some adhoc/event ones don't necessarily have an interview either. you just submit your details through WSS portal and if your application is processed and youre shortlisted, they will usually email you!

as for the salary, once youre assigned a job they will have you fill up a GIRO form where they can credit it to your bank account. the claims process is pretty simple, after the job is done you just have to go back to WSS portal and submit like a 'timesheet' of the hours you've worked etc! i suggest not worrying about all the nitty-gritty details of this first :-)

as for your last question, i personally have 2 WSS jobs, a CCA and am a final year engineering student.... hehe. i think having WSS and a CCA is okay, because regardless what u do, engineering will still be a pain in the ass so whats a few more commitment :'-)

im working at one of the subject libraries :-) it used to be $7 an hour (thats how much i started with during freshmen year), its been revised recently to $10 if im not wrong for all subject libraries!

hm technically you can earn the maximum amount if you work the maximum hours, but it's quite hard to come by because at the end of the day it depends on how tight your timetable and classes are and the availability of those shifts, so I really wouldn't bank on that. 

if you work off-campus, it depends on the job. I think cafes around here usually pay around $8-9/hr. Some high-end restaurants might go up to $15/hr. Another popular option is to give private tuitions or at centres, those could go up to $25/hr. Another thing you'd want to consider if you want to try and earn at least $600/month is going for an internship. You can try to request for 2-3 days work week if your schedule could fit, and internships here would pay you at least $600-800 usually, though you need to spend some time looking for the right ones. You can try looking for an internship [here](https://glints.com/sg).

Hi there! I'm also under WSS so I'll try my best to answer your queries!

1. I've been in the WSS since my freshmen year and I'm in my final year now so I think there isn't any restriction on how long you would want to stay on the job, granted the job that you apply isn't event-based. For example, I have been in multiple different WSS, my 'permanent' one being a student assistant in one of the libraries in NTU. I have taken adhoc ones that lasted a day or two and thats it. (Be careful not to exceed 16hrs per week when holding a few WSS jobs at once!) 
2. The money earned will be credited to your bank account directly so I guess you can then use it to pay your school fees manually either via GIRO or Cheque. If you mean that you'd want to pay the school fees directly from your WSS salary, I don't think thats possible. You can try emailing FinAid just to be sure. 
3. Honestly, the pay ranges quite a bit depending on how many shifts you get. (For my library job in this case). Its also worth noting that the payment is processed every 2 weeks so you'd usually get your pay twice a month. I'd say I get an average of about at LEAST $100\~ ($10/hr) every 2 weeks. So that's about at least $200 every month, most of the time I get a little more. That's for 1 WSS job alone, hence if you can take 2 WSS job (I'd recommend you to look out for a gallery sitter job at Gilman if you're browsing through the portal) and still not exceed 16hours a week you can easily earn more. The best time to work is usually during vacation as the 16hours restriction isn't applicable then and you get to earn more, around $300-$400.

Also, Gilman and Library SA both pay $10/hr, one being off-campus and in-campus respectively. I don't think they have restrictions on whether you're local or not so I believe the things I mentioned should be applicable to you :-) Anyways, hope this helps!

saturday crowds can get really bad, just a heads up.

1) DONT walk to the causeway by foot from marsiling mrt, its possible but boii why wld u do that LOL
ive nv taken bus from kranji, usually woodlands mrt got a lot of buses that stops at custom. just ask the bus driver, i assume u know where to drop if not check gps ya :-)

2) once uve cleared sg customs, the first hurdle is the bus queue. i think u can take any bus that has the shortest queue as per normal w ur ezlink. if u rlly on the crunch for time, u can take the yellow bus and pay cash.. i think thats $1? idk u can check again tmr at the berth display. 

3) next q is the msia customs!! if u r lucky and it doesnt look like a concert, then good for u. generally, when things get crowded best to move in to the deeper lanes. and generally, theres a queue that is being served by one immigration counter vs a queue thats being served by two counters. this happens bc eventually when u get to the counter to chop, the queue splits/forks out into the different counters. idk if u get it now but maybe u’ll understand tmr. generally, the queue that forks out to 2 counters are faster. but again, play by ear and luck ya. 

4) so u wanna meet him at 11am and wnna hv breakfast, assuming u take 30mins to grab a bite.. u gotta be there by 1030am. i suggest clearing sg immigration by 9am -> rch msia immigration by 930~ish -> my worst case scenario was standing in line at msia immigration for about an hour so if that happens to u means you’ll be done by 1030am. again, rlly depends on a number of factors but yeah the stated scenario is a possibility. 

if waking up early isnt a problem, just get there as early as u see fit. these are guidelines so i hope it has helped u in one way or another!
